claims.summary: Over any field, for the product pigeonhole system (m pigeons, n>=1 holes, multilinear ring) at degree D<=n and errors E_j of degree <=e, in the inert range (K+e<=D<n, or K+e<=n-1 at D=n): restriction to the set Y of hole-respecting assignments identifies V_K/(C cap V_K) with V_K|_Y, the common kernel with the zero set of restriction to the union S of the supports on Y, and the stacked rank with dim V_K|_S. If S = A x (all states of the other n-t holes), dim V_K|_S = sum_{s<=K} binom(n-t,s) m^s d_A(K-s), d_A(a)=dim V_a|_A; a monomial on e distinct holes has kernel dimension sum_{k<=K}[binom(n,k)-binom(n-e,k)] m^k, and the common kernel of x_(i,0), i in a set of size sigma, at K=1 has dimension m+1-sigma. At D=n, c of degree <=n lies in C iff c|_Y is in the span P_Y of the unplaced-pigeon indicators; for K+e<=n and K<=n-1 the stacked rank lies between dim V_K|_S - sum_j dim P_Y^{S_j} and dim V_K|_S.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer; the exact inert range and the top-degree part are its corrections.
claims.rationale: In the inert range the product pigeonhole system shows only union-of-supports savings; the top degree, where the record's non-inheritance example lives, is reduced to the unplaced-pigeon span.
